title: Partitioning Into Minimum Number Of Deci-Binary Numbers
summary: Given a string representing a positive decimal integer, determine the least count of positive deci-binary numbers whose sum equals the given integer.
statement: Given a string representing a positive decimal integer, determine the least count of positive deci-binary numbers whose sum equals the given integer. A deci-binary number consists solely of the digits 0 and 1.
constraints: n is a positive decimal string.
A deci-binary summand uses only digits zero and one; return the fewest positive summands whose decimal sum is n.
reference_solution:
def minimum_decibinary_parts(n):
 return max(int(digit) for digit in n)
hints: Each summand contributes at most one in any digit column.
The largest decimal digit is both a lower bound and achievable count.
Return max digit. Constructively, place a one in the first d summands for a column containing d.
The construction represents every column without carries using exactly the maximum digit number of summands.
editorial: The construction represents every column without carries using exactly the maximum digit number of summands.

tests.explanation: At least three summands are needed for digit three, and three suffice.
The digit eight forces eight summands.
